ios.desc:
Regularly gives you five original puzzles a day, one from each game. A new set arrives every morning, so there is always something waiting and always a reason to come back.

No streaks to keep alive, no clock ticking at you. Just a few quiet minutes of logic, words, and mental math to get your head going.

FIVE PUZZLES, EVERY DAY

Kingly. Place one king in every row, column, and color region, and never let two touch. Gentle logic in the spirit of Queens and Sudoku.

Countable. Combine the number tiles with + - x ÷ to hit the target. Quick mental math that is never the same twice.

Floored. Trace the hidden words and the letters cascade down, so the board shifts under you with every move. Half word search, half falling blocks.

Paths. Add light bulbs until every square is lit. Numbered walls tell you how many bulbs belong beside them. A bright take on light-up logic (Akari).

Thred. Follow a path through the letters to spell each hidden word. A word search with a thread to pull.

A HABIT THAT FITS YOUR DAY

Play on the train, over coffee, or just before bed. Finish the set, share how you did, and see how your friends got on.

WHAT YOU GET

A brand new set every single day. Five different puzzles across logic, words, and numbers. Results you can share. And a clean, calm design that stays out of your way.

Regularly speaks English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, and Chinese (Simplified).

Play one puzzle today. You will probably stay for all five.

quotes.text:
Several of my friends and family members are playing Countable, which is completely ad-free on iOS (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/countable-daily-numbers-game/id1617532286) and Android (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pibbon.countable).

Full disclosure: I developed this app during Christmas '22 with the idea of offering only one challenging new puzzle/level each day. I believe that the focus on the level of difficulty makes a huge difference.
quotes.story_title: How does the New York Times make a game?

quotes.text:
Hi HN. I wanted to present to you Regularly (https://regularly.co), a daily logic/math puzzle website I made to scratch my own itch: can we have a fun and engaging puzzle app that doesn't eventually devolve into an iap blockaded mess? For background, a few years ago I released my first daily puzzle (Countable), which I made for my then-girlfriend (now wife) and me to play over morning coffee. One marriage and four games later, the full Regularly set was born: with no ads, no sign-up, no iaps. It spread by word of mouth and a few hundred people now play each day.

Our business model is simple: the daily puzzles will always be free (without ads). At some point I may charge a small amount to access and play the back catalogue, but the day's puzzles stay free forever. As with many other websites, a fresh puzzle set drops every morning. However, unlike those websites, every puzzle shown is hand-picked rather than whatever we can make, and we really focus on getting the difficulty right. We watch how real players actually perform each day (for transparency, we track games started vs games completed to do this) and keep re-tuning our difficulty to maximise engagement. The aim is that every morning's set sits in the zone where you have to think but you aren't stumped.
